headline: High: dexter’s broad egress and API access make shared-workspace leakage and unsafe cross-agent action paths plausible, while awesome-nlp adds no isolation or verification.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: dexter has a writable scratchpad and autonomous execution, so if awesome-nlp content is copied into that workspace or parsed as instructions, prompt injection is plausible. awesome-nlp itself has no I/O surfaces, so the bridge is one-way and depends on external handling, not a built-in channel.
conditions: IF awesome-nlp outputs are copied into .dexter/scratchpad/
IF dexter treats scratchpad text as instructions or tool directives
mitigations: Keep awesome-nlp outputs out of dexter scratchpad
Prefix imported text as data, not instructions
Add a manual review step before any dexter tool call
Use separate workspaces for the two agents
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for imported content

B_data_leakage.rationale: dexter touches financial and market data and calls multiple third-party APIs, while awesome-nlp has no network egress and no data classes touched. If they share a workspace, dexter can ingest files from that workspace and transmit derived context externally, creating a plausible leakage path from shared files into third-party services.
conditions: IF both agents share the same filesystem workspace
IF dexter reads files from that workspace before calling external APIs
mitigations: Use separate directories for each agent
Remove sensitive files from dexter's workspace
Disable API calls during shared-file review
Rotate or scope API keys to least privilege
requires-engineering: enforce workspace ACLs

C_capability_conflict.rationale: awesome-nlp has no write surfaces, but dexter supports multiple instances and writes to .dexter/scratchpad/, so concurrent dexter runs can conflict with each other and with any shared files placed there. The pairwise conflict is not high because awesome-nlp itself is non-runnable and exposes no writes, but dexter’s mutable workspace still creates overlap risk.
conditions: IF two dexter instances run against the same .dexter/scratchpad/ directory
IF shared files are edited while dexter is running
mitigations: Run only one dexter instance per workspace
Give each run a unique scratchpad path
Avoid placing shared files in .dexter/scratchpad/
Check in-progress files before rerunning
requires-engineering: add file locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: dexter’s autonomous execution and API/tool use make it likely to act on upstream text, while awesome-nlp is a static repository/list with no verification layer. If awesome-nlp-derived content is fed into dexter, dexter may treat it as authoritative and propagate errors into research outputs or API-driven actions.
conditions: IF content from awesome-nlp is used as an input source for dexter
IF dexter does not verify claims before acting on them
mitigations: Require source verification before dexter acts
Mark awesome-nlp content as untrusted reference material
Add a human approval step for downstream actions
Cross-check claims against primary sources
requires-engineering: add citation validation

E_compliance.rationale: dexter explicitly touches financial and market data and uses third-party APIs, so compliance obligations can attach to its processing and retention. awesome-nlp is a static open-source list with no data handling, so it is not the compliance driver; the risk comes from dexter’s handling of regulated data classes and external services.
conditions: IF dexter processes regulated financial or market data
IF external API retention or logging exceeds policy
mitigations: Review API retention settings
Limit data sent to external APIs
Document data-class handling for dexter
Exclude regulated records from runs
requires-engineering: implement retention controls
